## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
```
:::



my_state = "CA"
my_variable = "B25064_001"

# lets find some data
ca_rent <-get_acs(
  geography = "county",
  variables = "B25064_001",
  state = "CA",
  year = 2023,
  survey = "acs5"
)

#we can view it like...

dim(ca_rent)
head(ca_rent)

#margin of error studies

ca_rent = ca_rent %>%
  mutate(moe_pct = as.numeric(moe) / as.numeric(estimate) * 100)
 
#lets take a look 
  
ca_rent %>%
  arrange(desc(moe_pct))%>%
  select (NAME, estimate, moe, moe_pct) %>%
  head (10)
  
ca_rent = ca_rent %>%
  mutate(reliability = case_when(
    moe_pct < 5 ~ "High confidence",
    moe_pct < 10 ~ "Moderate",
    TRUE        ~ "Low confidence"
))
count(ca_rent, reliability)

## Is the margin of error bigger in small places? go wide


ca_wide = get_acs (
  geography = "county",
  variables = c(myvar = "B25064_001",
                pop   = "B01003_001"),
  state = "CA",
  year  = 2023,
  survey = "acs5",
  output = "wide"
)
head(ca_wide)

names(ca_wide)


## lets do it with confidence

ca_wide = ca_wide %>%
  mutate(
  moe_pct = myvarM / myvarE * 100) %>%
  mutate(reliability = case_when (
           moe_pct < 5 ~ "High confidence",
          moe_pct < 15 ~ "Moderate", 
          TRUE         ~ "Low confidence"
  
))


ca_wide %>%
  group_by(reliability) %>%
  summarize(
  n_counties = n(),
  avg_population = mean(popE)
)
